parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ received: true, routed: true, service: $('Format Alert Message').first().json.service_name, anomaly_type: $('Format Alert Message').first().json.anomaly_type, confidence_score: $('Format Alert Message').first().json.confidence_score, telegram_sent: ($('Telegram Alert').first().json.result && $('Telegram Alert').first().json.ok) ?? null, email_sent: ($('Email Alert').first().json.data && true) ?? null }) }}

_comment.description: Sentinelas n8n anomaly alert routing workflow (Telegram + Email).
_comment.flow: Webhook -> IF confidence>=0.6 -> Format -> Telegram -> Email -> Respond (serial, so the webhook responds exactly once)
_comment.threshold_note: 0.6, not 0.7: the LightGBM model emits ~0.67 for clear anomalies, so a 0.7 gate suppressed genuine detections.
credentials_required: Sentinelas Alert Bot (telegramApi) — BotFather access token, id=sentinelas-telegram-bot
Gmail SMTP (smtp) — smtp.gmail.com:587, user=nourhanelshieikh71@gmail.com, 16-char Gmail App Password, id=sentinelas-gmail-smtp
_comment.why_not_vars: $vars (TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID / ALERT_*_EMAIL) is empty on this instance, so chatId and addresses are set inline; the bot token lives only in the encrypted credential.
